correctness.rationale: The Finding's inequalities, equality classes and rigidity are mathematically correct. For f=h_K² the intersection norm squared is the frame sum. The columns are exchangeable and orthogonal, not independent (correct the word 'independent' in RESULT.md:32); the proof uses their correct conditional law. Projection removes degrees zero and two, since these are exactly the restricted quadratics. For each even surviving degree 2m the covariance identity and equatorial average give multiplier d[1+(d−1)p_{d,2m}(0)]. The product ratio (2m+1)/(d+2m−1) is strictly less than one for d≥3. The extreme positive and negative equatorial eigenvalues on the residual space are at degrees four and six respectively, giving the constants and the equality spaces. Separately generating the normalized zonal polynomials via their differential equation (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 3) recovers the critical multipliers in symbolic dimension; this is a check, not the proof for every degree. The perturbations sqrt(1+εY) are support functions by positive definiteness of the spherical curvature operator for sufficiently small ε, and K is an ellipsoid iff the defect vanishes. No uploaded verifier was executed. There is also a false ancillary limitation in RESULT.md:56 (not needed for the Finding): the least-squares Q is globally positive definite here. Indeed for F(x)=h_K(x)^2 extended homogeneously and standard Gaussian G, the projection formula gives 2Q=E[F(G)(GGᵀ−I)]=E[D²F(G)], in the distributional integration-by-parts sense. F is convex and F(x)≥r²||x||² for an inscribed origin-centered ball of radius r>0. On any line its second derivative measure is positive and nonzero (the quadratic lower growth precludes an affine function); integration against the strictly positive Gaussian density gives vᵀQv>0 for every v≠0. Thus the warning about a nonpositive nearest quadratic does not describe an actual obstruction under the stated assumptions.
